notes.deviation_model_note: all three fits selected the same deviation grid member (index 394), consistent with the paper's finding that all three fits select the same deviation model (a near-random walk with a 3.5-year cycle); this shared member is used directly as the held-fixed deviation model for every simulated continuation and restricted refit below.
notes.n_observations_vs_paper: 819 weekly observations used here vs. the paper's 820 (see exp5.py docstring / results/RESULTS.md for the data-source substitution); everything else follows the paper's construction unchanged.
notes.simulation_count_reduced: config.SEPARATION_N_SIMULATIONS_RUN=150 requested (n_requested=150); 4 actually used per 'true' model (3 x 4 = 12 continuations total), instead of the paper's 1000, so that the full sweep (3 true models x 4 cutoffs x n_simulations_used continuations x up to 3 trend refits each, with the restricted single-member Gompertz refit as the main cost, timed at calibration) fits the computing-time budget. Pass --full to attempt the paper's count (very slow; not run here).
notes.gompertz_refit_simplification: the Gompertz refit at each cutoff uses a bespoke single-stage restricted search (_refit_gompertz_fixed_theta: one bounded L-BFGS-B call against the shared held-fixed deviation model's covariance, reusing exp.exp6._nonlinear_ll for the likelihood evaluation) instead of src.trend_models.fit_nonlinear_model or exp.exp6._fit_nonlinear_restricted verbatim, because both of those look up a multi-member-grid reference (a fixed 'random walk, no cycle' member) that need not exist in -- and, per the paper's own finding of a 3.5-year cycle in the shared deviation model, does not exist in -- a one-element restricted grid.
notes.future_volatility: future weekly volatility enters only through the declared deviation family's covariance at the shared, held-fixed deviation model; no separate volatility parameter is introduced here (consistent with exp6's convention).
